answer: When an AI‑agent submits a credential, the system assigns it to a random jury drawn from a meadow of verified nodes, each jury member receiving a zephyr‑light audit token. Periodically the inlet of spot‑check audits selects a subset of those tokens, forcing agents to reveal a proof‑of‑work stamp that costs the attacker computational cycles proportional to the number of jurors impersonated. Because each fake identity must survive independent audits, the expense grows linearly with the sybil count, making large‑scale attacks economically infeasible.
